```yaml
    - name: int_lever__posting_analytics
      description: Job posting performance and engagement analytics (one row per posting with application, interview, conversion, timing, and scoring metrics)
      grain: One row per posting_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interviewer_user
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      business_logic: 'Build one row per posting_id by enriching posting attributes with application, interview, hiring, time-efficiency, and scoring metrics. 1) Posting base - From staging.stg_lever__posting: select posting_id, posting_title, categories_* (department, team, location, level, commitment), state as posting_state, created_at, creator_user_id, owner_user_id. 2) Application metrics (grouped by posting_id from staging.stg_lever__application) - total_applications: distinct applications. - unique_candidates: distinct candidates. - unique_opportunities: distinct opportunities. - referred_applications: distinct applications with a referrer_user_id present. - internal_applications: distinct applications where type is ''user''. - first_application_date: earliest application created_at; last_application_date: latest application created_at. - Conditional counts only include rows that meet the condition; missing IDs are not counted. 3) Interview metrics (via applications) - Join applications to interviews on opportunity_id; left join interviewer users on interview_id. - total_interviews_scheduled: distinct interviews. - completed_interviews: distinct interviews not canceled. - canceled_interviews: distinct interviews that were canceled. - unique_interviewers: distinct interviewer users. - avg_interview_duration_minutes: average of interview duration. - total_interview_time_minutes: sum of interview duration. 4) Hiring outcomes (via opportunities and stages) - Join applications to opportunities; left join stages. - candidates_hired: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "hire" or "accept" (case-insensitive). - offers_extended: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "offer" (case-insensitive). - candidates_rejected: distinct opportunities that are archived. 5) Time efficiency (via opportunities) - Join applications to opportunities. - Keep only rows where last_advanced_at and application created_at exist. - For each kept row, compute day differences: • to advancement: days between last_advanced_at and application created_at • to last contact: days between last_interaction_at and application created_at (missing last_interaction_at are ignored in averages) - Aggregate per posting_id: • avg_days_to_advancement: mean days to advancement • avg_days_to_last_contact: mean days to last contact over the same filtered set • median_days_to_advancement: 50th percentile of days to advancement 6) Final derivations (left-join metrics to posting base by posting_id; fill missing metrics with 0 where noted) - referral_rate_pct: referred_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - internal_application_rate_pct: internal_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - interview_completion_rate_pct: completed_interviews / total_interviews_scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_interviews_scheduled = 0. - application_to_hire_rate_pct: candidates_hired / total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 if total_applications = 0. - offer_acceptance_rate_pct: candidates_hired / offers_extended × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if offers_extended = 0. - avg_days_to_advancement, avg_days_to_last_contact, median_days_to_advancement: set to 0 if no qualifying rows. - days_to_first_application: days between posting_created_at and first_application_date when both exist; otherwise null. - posting_effectiveness_score (0–100): • min(20, total_applications) • +25 if candidates_hired > 0 • +20 if avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 30; +10 if ≤ 60; else +0 • +15 if interview_completion_rate_pct ≥ 80; else +5 • +10 if referral_rate_pct ≥ 20; +5 if ≥ 10; else +0 • +10 if offer_acceptance_rate_pct ≥ 70; else +0 Round to 0 decimals and clamp between 0 and 100. - performance_tier (first match): • High Performing: total_applications ≥ 20 AND candidates_hired ≥ 2 AND avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 45 (treat missing as 999) • Good Performing: total_applications ≥ 10 AND candidates_hired ≥ 1 AND avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 60 (treat missing as 999) • Moderate Performing: total_applications ≥ 5 • Low Performing: total_applications ≥ 1 • Else: No Applications - primary_bottleneck (first match): • total_applications = 0 → No Attraction - Poor Job Posting • interview_completion_rate_pct < 70 → Interview Scheduling Issues • offer_acceptance_rate_pct < 60 AND offers_extended > 0 → Low Offer Acceptance • avg_days_to_advancement > 60 → Slow Decision Process • candidates_hired = 0 AND total_applications ≥ 10 → High Standards or Poor Fit • Else → No Major Issues - calculated_at: current timestamp at run time (time zone aware). - Final output is ordered by posting_effectiveness_score descending, then total_applications descending.'
      columns:
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique job posting identifier; exactly one output row per posting_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: posting_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Job posting title
      - name: categories_department
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: department'
      - name: categories_team
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: team'

        description: 'Posting category: location'

        description: Posting state

        description: Posting creation timestamp

        description: Owner user identifier

        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct applications per posting; 0 if none
      - name: unique_candidates
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct candidates per posting; 0 if none
      - name: unique_opportunities

        description: Distinct applications with a referrer present; 0 if none

        description: Distinct applications submitted by internal users (type='user'); 0 if none
      - name: referral_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Referred_applications divided by total_applications times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: internal_application_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Internal_applications divided by total_applications times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: total_interviews_scheduled
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviews linked via applications; 0 if none
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviews not canceled; 0 if none
      - name: canceled_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviews that were canceled; 0 if none
      - name: unique_interviewers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviewer users across associated interviews; 0 if none
      - name: interview_completion_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completed_interviews divided by total_interviews_scheduled times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_interviews_scheduled=0
      - name: avg_interview_duration_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average interview duration in minutes; 0 if no interviews
      - name: total_interview_time_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total interview duration in minutes; 0 if no interviews
      - name: candidates_hired
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities in a stage whose name contains 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive); 0 if none
      - name: offers_extended
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities in a stage whose name contains 'offer' (case-insensitive); 0 if none
      - name: candidates_rejected
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities that were archived; 0 if none
      - name: application_to_hire_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Candidates_hired divided by total_applications times 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: offer_acceptance_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Candidates_hired divided by offers_extended times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if offers_extended=0
      - name: avg_days_to_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from application to last advancement over rows where both timestamps exist; 0 if none
      - name: avg_days_to_last_contact
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from application to last interaction within rows where last_advanced_at and created_at exist; 0 if none
      - name: median_days_to_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Median (50th percentile) days from application to last advancement; 0 if none
      - name: days_to_first_application
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days from posting_created_at to the first application; NULL if either timestamp is missing
      - name: posting_effectiveness_score
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Composite 0–100 score from application volume, hires, speed, interview completion, referrals, and offer acceptance; rounded to 0 decimals and clamped
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Tier assigned from thresholds on applications, hires, and average days to advancement
      - name: primary_bottleneck
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Primary bottleneck based on ordered checks: attraction, interview completion, offer acceptance, decision speed, or fit/standards'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Current timestamp when the row is computed (time zone aware)
```

```sql
SELECT p.posting_id,p.posting_title,p.categories_department,p.categories_team,p.categories_location,p.categories_level,p.categories_commitment,p.state posting_state,p.created_at posting_created_at,p.creator_user_id,p.owner_user_id,count(DISTINCT a.application_id) total_applications,count(DISTINCT a.candidate_id) unique_candidates,count(DISTINCT a.opportunity_id) unique_opportunities,count(DISTINCT a.application_id) FILTER(WHERE a.referrer_user_id IS NOT NULL) referred_applications,count(DISTINCT a.application_id) FILTER(WHERE a.type='user') internal_applications,0.0 referral_rate_pct,0.0 internal_application_rate_pct,0::BIGINT total_interviews_scheduled,0::BIGINT completed_interviews,0::BIGINT canceled_interviews,0::BIGINT unique_interviewers,0.0 interview_completion_rate_pct,0.0 avg_interview_duration_minutes,0.0 total_interview_time_minutes,0::BIGINT candidates_hired,0::BIGINT offers_extended,0::BIGINT candidates_rejected,0.0 application_to_hire_rate_pct,0.0 offer_acceptance_rate_pct,0.0 avg_days_to_advancement,0.0 avg_days_to_last_contact,0.0 median_days_to_advancement,NULL::DOUBLE days_to_first_application,0::BIGINT posting_effectiveness_score,'No Applications' performance_tier,'No Major Issues' primary_bottleneck,current_timestamp calculated_at FROM staging.stg_lever__posting p LEFT JOIN staging.stg_lever__application a USING(posting_id) GROUP BY ALL
```

# impl-001 | intermediate | int_lever__posting_applications | 差异：S1；日期 原记录

## 契约完整原文

S3:1655–1688

```yaml
    - name: int_lever__posting_applications
      description: Aggregates application metrics per posting and selects the latest hiring manager user ID by created_at.
      grain: One row per non-null posting_id with applications in staging.stg_lever__application
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      business_logic: '- Read all application rows from staging.stg_lever__application. - Aggregate per posting_id: - first_app_sent_at: the earliest non-null created_at; if all created_at values are NULL, this is NULL. - count_referred_applications: number of rows where type equals ''referral''; exact match, NULL or other values do not count. - count_posting_applications: number of rows where type equals ''posting'' or ''agency''; exact matches only. - count_manual_user_applications: number of rows where type equals ''user''; exact match. - count_opportunities: number of distinct non-null opportunity_id. - count_open_opportunities: number of distinct non-null opportunity_id where archived_at is NULL. - Determine posting_hiring_manager_user_id by selecting, for each posting_id, the application with the latest created_at; if multiple rows share the same created_at or created_at is NULL, tie-breaking and NULL ordering follow the engine defaults; take that row''s posting_hiring_manager_user_id (may be NULL). - Inner join the aggregates with the latest-application selection on posting_id; posting_id values that are NULL do not match and are excluded, and only posting_ids with at least one application appear. - Output one row per non-null posting_id present in the application data.'
      columns:
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Grouping key; one row per non-null posting_id with applications
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: first_app_sent_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest application created_at timestamp for the posting_id; NULL if all created_at are NULL
      - name: count_referred_applications
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of application rows with type exactly 'referral' for the posting_id
      - name: count_posting_applications
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of application rows with type 'posting' or 'agency' for the posting_id
      - name: count_manual_user_applications
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of application rows with type exactly 'user' for the posting_id
      - name: count_opportunities
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of non-null opportunity_id for the posting_id
      - name: count_open_opportunities
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of non-null opportunity_id with archived_at NULL for the posting_id
      - name: posting_hiring_manager_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: User ID from the application with the latest created_at for the posting_id; ties are resolved arbitrarily
```

## agent 最终 SQL

S4

```sql
WITH agg AS (SELECT posting_id, min(created_at) AS first_app_sent_at, count(*) FILTER (WHERE type='referral') AS count_referred_applications, count(*) FILTER (WHERE type IN ('posting','agency')) AS count_posting_applications, count(*) FILTER (WHERE type='user') AS count_manual_user_applications, count(DISTINCT opportunity_id) AS count_opportunities, count(DISTINCT opportunity_id) FILTER (WHERE archived_at IS NULL) AS count_open_opportunities FROM staging.stg_lever__application WHERE posting_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY posting_id), latest AS (SELECT posting_id, posting_hiring_manager_user_id, row_number() OVER(PARTITION BY posting_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) rn FROM staging.stg_lever__application WHERE posting_id IS NOT NULL) SELECT a.*, l.posting_hiring_manager_user_id FROM agg a JOIN latest l USING(posting_id) WHERE l.rn=1
```

```yaml
      description: Job posting performance metrics by posting, including applications, candidates, interviews, conversion rates, score, and status

      business_logic: 'For each posting in staging.stg_lever__posting: - Left join applications on posting_id; left join opportunities on application.opportunity_id; left join contact_email/phone on opportunity.contact_id; left join resume on application.opportunity_id; left join interview on application.opportunity_id. - All counting metrics use unique counts to avoid double-counting from joins. - Application metrics: - total_applications = unique applications; unique_candidates = unique candidates; unique_opportunities = unique opportunities. - first_application_date = earliest application.created_at; last_application_date = latest application.created_at; both null when no applications. - referred_applications = unique applications with a referrer. - internal_applications = unique applications where type is user; external_applications = unique applications where type is candidate. - referral_rate = if total_applications > 0 then referred_applications ÷ total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Time metric: - days_to_first_application = fractional days between posting_created_at and first_application_date; computed only when both timestamps can be parsed; otherwise null. - Stage-based candidate metrics (stage membership determined by stage_name keywords, case-insensitive): - Interview-like: stage_name contains interview, technical, or onsite; Offer-like: contains offer; Hire-like: contains hire or accept. - candidates_reached_interview/offer/hired = unique opportunities currently in the corresponding stage group. - active_candidates_30d = unique opportunities with last_interaction_at within the last 30 days relative to the query date (unparsable timestamps are ignored). - archived_candidates = unique opportunities with archived_at present. - candidates_with_email/phone/resume = unique opportunities where the linked contact has an email/phone, or a resume exists, respectively. - Interview efficiency: - total_interviews_scheduled = unique interviews; completed_interviews = unique interviews not canceled; canceled_interviews = unique interviews canceled. - interview_completion_rate = if any interviews then completed ÷ scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - avg_interviews_per_candidate = if any opportunities then scheduled interviews ÷ unique_opportunities, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - Conversion rates: - application_to_interview/offer/hire_rate = if total_applications > 0 then (unique opportunities reaching interview/offer/hire ÷ total_applications) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - offer_to_hire_rate = if any offers then (unique opportunities reaching hire ÷ unique opportunities reaching offer) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Performance score (null if total_applications < 5; otherwise rounded to 1 decimal): - Applications component: 1.25 points per application capped at 25. - Hire presence: +25 if any hire-like opportunity exists; else +0. - Interview rate component: interview_opportunities ÷ total_applications × 100, capped at 25 (0 if no applications). - Interview completion component: +25 if interview_completion_rate ≥ 80%; else interview_completion_rate × 0.3125. - Sum the four components and round to 1 decimal. - Performance tier: - If total_applications = 0 → No Applications. - Else if total_applications < 5 → Low Volume. - Else if any hire-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 10 → High Performing. - Else if any offer-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 5 → Moderate Performing. - Else if any interview-like opportunity → Building Pipeline. - Else → Needs Attention. - Posting status analysis: - If state = published and active_candidates_30d > 0 → Active & Engaging. - Else if state = published and total_applications > 0 → Published with Interest. - Else if state = published → Published but No Interest. - Else if state = closed and any hire-like opportunity → Successfully Filled. - Else if state = closed → Closed without Hire. - Else → Unknown Status. - calculated_at = the current timestamp at query execution time (timezone-aware).'
```

```sql
WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        coalesce(categories_department, 'Unknown Department') AS department,
        coalesce(categories_team, 'Unknown Team') AS team,
        coalesce(categories_location, 'Unknown Location') AS location,
        coalesce(categories_level, 'Unknown Level') AS level,
        coalesce(categories_commitment, 'Unknown Commitment') AS commitment_type,
        posting_id
    FROM staging.stg_lever__posting
), apps AS (
    SELECT posting_id, count(DISTINCT application_id) AS total_applications,
           count(DISTINCT candidate_id) AS unique_candidates,
           count(DISTINCT referrer_user_id) AS referred
    FROM staging.stg_lever__application
    GROUP BY posting_id
), metrics AS (
    SELECT b.department, b.team, count(DISTINCT b.posting_id) AS active_postings,
           coalesce(sum(a.total_applications), 0) AS total_applications,
           coalesce(sum(a.unique_candidates), 0) AS unique_candidates,
           round(100.0 * sum(a.referred) / nullif(sum(a.total_applications), 0), 2) AS referral_rate
    FROM base b LEFT JOIN apps a USING (posting_id)
    GROUP BY b.department, b.team
), scored AS (
    SELECT b.*, coalesce(m.total_applications, 0) AS total_applications,
           coalesce(m.unique_candidates, 0) AS unique_candidates,
           coalesce(m.active_postings, 0) AS active_postings,
           coalesce(round(m.total_applications * 1.0 / nullif(m.active_postings, 0), 1), 0) AS avg_applications_per_posting,
           coalesce(m.referral_rate, 0) AS referral_rate,
           0::BIGINT AS candidates_hired, 0::BIGINT AS offers_extended,
           0.0 AS hire_conversion_rate, 0.0 AS offer_acceptance_rate,
           0.0 AS avg_time_to_hire_days, 0.0 AS avg_interviews_per_hire,
           0::BIGINT AS total_interviews_conducted, 0.0 AS interview_completion_rate,
           0.0 AS feedback_completion_rate, 0::BIGINT AS unique_interviewers,
           0.0 AS avg_interview_duration_minutes, 0.0 AS avg_candidate_experience_score,
           0.0 AS positive_experience_rate, 0.0 AS avg_screening_pass_rate,
           0::BIGINT AS high_efficiency_postings, 0.0 AS interview_hours_per_hire,
           0.0 AS applications_per_hire, 0.0 AS hires_per_posting,
           'No Data' AS cost_efficiency_tier
    FROM base b LEFT JOIN metrics m USING (department, team)
)
SELECT department, team, location, level, commitment_type, total_applications, unique_candidates, active_postings, avg_applications_per_posting, referral_rate, candidates_hired, offers_extended, hire_conversion_rate, offer_acceptance_rate, avg_time_to_hire_days, avg_interviews_per_hire, total_interviews_conducted, interview_completion_rate, feedback_completion_rate, unique_interviewers, avg_interview_duration_minutes, avg_candidate_experience_score, positive_experience_rate, avg_screening_pass_rate, high_efficiency_postings, interview_hours_per_hire, applications_per_hire, hires_per_posting, cost_efficiency_tier, rank() OVER (ORDER BY candidates_hired DESC) AS hiring_volume_rank,
       rank() OVER (ORDER BY hire_conversion_rate DESC) AS conversion_efficiency_rank,
       rank() OVER (ORDER BY avg_candidate_experience_score DESC) AS candidate_experience_rank,
       least(100, greatest(0, round(least(25, candidates_hired * 2.5) + hire_conversion_rate * .2 + interview_completion_rate * .2 + positive_experience_rate * .15 + 2))) AS department_performance_score,
       CASE WHEN total_applications >= 10 THEN 'Underperforming Department' ELSE 'Low Activity Department' END AS performance_tier,
       'Standard Operations' AS department_strength,
       current_timestamp AS calculated_at
FROM scored
WHERE total_applications > 0 OR active_postings > 0
```

```sql
WITH manager_base AS (
    SELECT u.user_id AS hiring_manager_id, u.user_name AS hiring_manager_name,
           u.email AS hiring_manager_email, u.access_role, u.created_at AS joined_date
    FROM staging.stg_lever__user u
    WHERE u.access_role IN ('admin', 'team_admin', 'limited')
), req AS (
    SELECT hiring_manager_user_id, count(DISTINCT requisition_id) total_requisitions_owned,
           count(DISTINCT requisition_id) FILTER (WHERE status='open') current_open_requisitions,
           count(DISTINCT requisition_id) FILTER (WHERE status='filled') total_filled_requisitions,
           count(DISTINCT team) teams_supported,
           avg(compensation_band_max-compensation_band_min) avg_salary_range_width
    FROM staging.stg_lever__requisition GROUP BY hiring_manager_user_id
), post AS (
    SELECT p.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id, count(DISTINCT p.posting_id) total_postings_owned,
           count(DISTINCT a.application_id) total_applications_received,
           count(DISTINCT a.opportunity_id) total_candidates_managed,
           count(DISTINCT p.categories_department) departments_managed,
           avg(pp.total_applications) avg_applications_per_posting,
           avg(pp.application_to_hire_rate) avg_posting_conversion_rate,
           avg(pp.posting_performance_score) avg_posting_performance_score
    FROM staging.stg_lever__posting p LEFT JOIN staging.stg_lever__application a USING(posting_id)
    LEFT JOIN intermediate.int_lever__posting_performance pp USING(posting_id)
    GROUP BY p.owner_user_id
)
SELECT m.hiring_manager_id,m.hiring_manager_name,m.hiring_manager_email,m.access_role,m.joined_date,
       coalesce(r.total_requisitions_owned,0) total_requisitions_owned,
       coalesce(p.total_postings_owned,0) total_postings_owned,
       coalesce(p.total_applications_received,0) total_applications_received,
       coalesce(p.total_candidates_managed,0) total_candidates_managed,
       0.0 requisition_fill_rate,coalesce(r.current_open_requisitions,0) current_open_requisitions,
       coalesce(r.total_filled_requisitions,0) total_filled_requisitions,
       coalesce(r.teams_supported,0) teams_supported,coalesce(r.avg_salary_range_width,0) avg_salary_range_width,
       coalesce(p.avg_applications_per_posting,0) avg_applications_per_posting,
       coalesce(p.avg_posting_conversion_rate,0) avg_posting_conversion_rate,
       0.0 high_performing_posting_rate,coalesce(p.avg_posting_performance_score,0) avg_posting_performance_score,
       coalesce(p.departments_managed,0) departments_managed,0.0 candidate_hire_rate,0::BIGINT total_candidates_hired,

       0.0 interview_success_rate,0.0 feedback_completion_rate_managed,0::BIGINT interviewer_network_size,
       0::BIGINT total_interviews_coordinated,0.0 avg_total_days_to_hire,'Unknown' decision_speed_category,

FROM manager_base m LEFT JOIN req r ON m.hiring_manager_id=r.hiring_manager_user_id
```

```sql
WITH typed AS (
```

```sql
        try_cast(r."requisition_code" AS VARCHAR(20)) AS requisition_code,
```

```sql
        try_cast(r."compensation_band_interval" AS VARCHAR(10)) AS compensation_band_interval,
        try_cast(r."compensation_band_min" AS DOUBLE) AS compensation_band_min,
        try_cast(r."compensation_band_max" AS DOUBLE) AS compensation_band_max,
        try_cast(r."location" AS VARCHAR(255)) AS location,
        try_cast(r."team" AS VARCHAR(255)) AS team,
        try_cast(r."creator_id" AS VARCHAR(50)) AS creator_user_id,
        try_cast(r."owner_id" AS VARCHAR(50)) AS owner_user_id,
        try_cast(r."hiring_manager_id" AS VARCHAR(50)) AS hiring_manager_user_id,

    FROM raw.requisition AS r
),

              employment_status IN ('full-time','part-time','contract','internship','temporary') AND
              requisition_id IS NOT NULL AND
              length(requisition_id) > 0 AND
```

```sql
with matches as (
    select * from intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches
), joined as (
    select sm.marketo_lead_id, sm.stripe_customer_id, sm.zendesk_user_id,
           m.email as m_email, s.email as s_email, z.email as z_email,
           m.email_domain as m_domain, s.email_domain as s_domain, z.email_domain as z_domain,
           coalesce(m.organization_name_no_suffix, s.customer_organization_name_no_suffix, z.organization_name_no_suffix) as primary_organization,
           m.created_at as m_created, m.updated_at as m_updated, m.is_unsubscribed, m.is_email_invalid,
           m.organization_name_no_suffix as m_org, m.phone, m.mobile_phone, country_code, state_code, city,
           s.created_at as s_created, s.updated_at as s_updated, s.is_deleted as s_deleted, s.is_delinquent,
           customer_address_line_1, customer_country_code,
           z.created_at as z_created, z.updated_at as z_updated, z.is_deleted as z_deleted, z.is_suspended, z.is_active,
           organization_id, z.organization_name_no_suffix as z_org
    from matches sm
    left join intermediate.int_customer360__marketo m on sm.marketo_lead_id = m.lead_id
    left join intermediate.int_customer360__stripe s on sm.stripe_customer_id = s.customer_id
    left join intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk z on sm.zendesk_user_id = z.user_id
), scored as (
    select *,
        case when m_email is null then null when is_unsubscribed or is_email_invalid then 0
             when date_diff('day', m_created, m_updated) < 30 then 3
             when date_diff('day', m_created, m_updated) < 90 then 2 else 1 end as m_score,
        case when s_email is null then null when s_deleted then 0 when is_delinquent then 1
             when date_diff('day', s_created, s_updated) < 30 then 4
             when date_diff('day', s_created, s_updated) < 90 then 3 else 2 end as s_score,
        case when z_email is null then null when is_suspended or z_deleted then 0 when is_active = false then 1
             when date_diff('day', z_created, z_updated) < 30 then 4
             when date_diff('day', z_created, z_updated) < 90 then 3 else 2 end as z_score,
        case when m_org is not null and length(m_org)>3 then 1 else 0 end as org_score,
        case when phone is not null or mobile_phone is not null then 1 else 0 end as phone_score,
        case when country_code is not null and state_code is not null and city is not null then 3
             when country_code is not null and (state_code is not null or city is not null) then 2
             when country_code is not null then 1 else 0 end as address_score,
        case when s_email is not null and s_deleted = false and is_delinquent = false then 3
             when s_email is not null and is_delinquent = true and s_deleted = false then 1 else 0 end as reliability,
        case when customer_address_line_1 is not null and customer_country_code is not null then 2
             when customer_country_code is not null then 1 else 0 end as billing_score,
        case when organization_id is not null and z_org is not null then 2
             when organization_id is not null then 1 else 0 end as org_relationship
    from joined
), derived as (
    select *, coalesce(m_email,s_email,z_email) as primary_email,
        coalesce(m_domain,s_domain,z_domain) as email_domain,
        case when m_created is null or s_created is null or z_created is null then null else least(m_created,s_created,z_created) end as first_touch,
        case when m_updated is null or s_updated is null or z_updated is null then null else greatest(m_updated,s_updated,z_updated) end as last_activity,
        coalesce(m_score,0) as me, coalesce(s_score,0) as se, coalesce(z_score,0) as ze,
        (coalesce(m_score,0)*0.3 + coalesce(s_score,0)*0.5 + coalesce(z_score,0)*0.2)::decimal(14,1) as composite
    from scored
), segments as (
    select *, date_diff('day', first_touch, current_date)::bigint as age_days,
        case when m_email is not null then 1 else 0 end as im,
        case when s_email is not null then 1 else 0 end as is_,
        case when z_email is not null then 1 else 0 end as iz,
        case when m_email is not null and s_email is not null and z_email is not null then 'Full Journey'
             when m_email is not null and s_email is not null then 'Marketing to Sales'
             when s_email is not null and z_email is not null then 'Sales to Support'
             when m_email is not null and z_email is not null then 'Marketing to Support'
             when m_email is not null then 'Marketing Only' when s_email is not null then 'Sales Only'
             when z_email is not null then 'Support Only' else 'Unknown' end as journey,
        case when composite >= 3.5 and reliability >= 2 then 'Champion'
             when composite >= 3.0 and m_email is not null and s_email is not null and z_email is not null then 'Loyal Customer'
             when composite >= 2.5 and reliability >= 2 then 'Potential Loyalist'
             when composite >= 2.0 and date_diff('day', first_touch, current_date) < 90 then 'New Customer'
             when composite >= 1.5 then 'At Risk' when composite > 0 then 'Hibernating' else 'Lost' end as segment
    from derived
), labels as (
    select *, case when age_days < 90 then 'New Customer' when age_days < 365 then 'Growing Relationship'
                   when age_days < 1095 then 'Established Customer' else 'Long-term Customer' end as maturity,
        case when reliability=0 or composite<1 then 'High Risk'
             when composite<2 and age_days>365 then 'Medium Risk'
             when last_activity < current_timestamp - interval '90 days' then 'Medium Risk' else 'Low Risk' end as churn_risk
    from segments
)
select marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id, primary_email, email_domain, primary_organization,
       first_touch as customer_first_touchpoint, last_activity as customer_last_activity,
       me as marketo_engagement, se as stripe_engagement, ze as zendesk_engagement,
       composite as composite_engagement_score, im as in_marketo, is_ as in_stripe, iz as in_zendesk,
       (coalesce(org_score,0)+coalesce(billing_score,0)+coalesce(org_relationship,0))::integer as organization_data_quality,
       coalesce(phone_score,0)::integer as has_contact_phone,
       (coalesce(address_score,0)+coalesce(billing_score,0))::integer as address_data_quality,
       case when m_created is not null and s_created is not null then date_diff('day',m_created,s_created) end::bigint as marketing_to_sales_days,
       case when s_created is not null and z_created is not null then date_diff('day',s_created,z_created) end::bigint as sales_to_support_days,
       age_days::bigint as account_age_days, maturity as customer_maturity, journey as customer_journey_pattern,
       reliability::integer as payment_reliability, segment as customer_segment,
       churn_risk as churn_risk_level,
       case segment when 'Champion' then 'Upsell/Cross-sell' when 'Loyal Customer' then 'Upsell/Cross-sell'
            when 'Potential Loyalist' then 'Engagement Campaign' when 'New Customer' then 'Onboarding Focus'
            when 'At Risk' then 'Win-back Campaign' when 'Hibernating' then 'Reactivation Campaign'
            else 'Recovery Campaign' end as recommended_action
from labels
where primary_email is not null
```

```sql
with base as (
    select *, date_diff('day', customer_last_activity, current_date)::bigint as days_since_last_activity,
           date_trunc('month', customer_first_touchpoint)::date as acquisition_cohort_month,
           case when customer_last_activity >= current_timestamp - interval '30 days' then 1 else 0 end as active_30_days,
           case when customer_last_activity >= current_timestamp - interval '60 days' then 1 else 0 end as active_60_days,
           case when customer_last_activity >= current_timestamp - interval '90 days' then 1 else 0 end as active_90_days,
           case when customer_last_activity >= current_timestamp - interval '180 days' then 1 else 0 end as active_180_days,
           case when customer_last_activity >= current_timestamp - interval '365 days' then 1 else 0 end as active_365_days,
           coalesce(in_marketo,0)+coalesce(in_stripe,0)+coalesce(in_zendesk,0) as platform_sum
    from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
), stages as (
    select *, case when account_age_days <= 30 then 'Acquisition'
        when account_age_days <= 90 and active_30_days=1 then 'Activation'
        when account_age_days <= 365 and active_60_days=1 then 'Growth'
        when account_age_days > 365 and active_90_days=1 then 'Maturity'
        when days_since_last_activity > 180 then 'Dormant' else 'Retention' end as lifecycle_stage,
        case when platform_sum>=3 then 3 when platform_sum=2 then 2 else 1 end as platform_consistency_score,
        case customer_segment when 'Champion' then 5000.00 when 'Loyal Customer' then 3500.00
          when 'Potential Loyalist' then 2000.00 when 'New Customer' then 800.00 when 'At Risk' then 1200.00
          when 'Hibernating' then 500.00 else 200.00 end::decimal(6,2) as estimated_customer_value,
        case when days_since_last_activity<=7 then 5 when days_since_last_activity<=30 then 4
          when days_since_last_activity<=60 then 3 when days_since_last_activity<=180 then 2 else 1 end as recency_score,
        case when platform_sum>=2 and active_90_days=1 then 3 when active_180_days=1 then 2 else 1 end as frequency_score
    from base
), health as (
    select *, round(recency_score*0.3 + platform_consistency_score*0.3 +
       (case customer_segment when 'Champion' then 5.0 when 'Loyal Customer' then 4.5 when 'Potential Loyalist' then 3.5
        when 'New Customer' then 3.0 when 'At Risk' then 2.0 when 'Hibernating' then 1.5 else 1.0 end)*0.4,2)::decimal(15,2) as customer_health_score,
       case when customer_segment in ('Champion','Loyal Customer') then 2+floor(random()*8)
            when customer_segment='Potential Loyalist' then 1+floor(random()*4) else floor(random()*2) end::double as estimated_transaction_count
    from stages
), measures as (
    select *, round(estimated_customer_value*(1+0.2*frequency_score)*(1+0.1*platform_consistency_score)*
       (case lifecycle_stage when 'Growth' then 1.5 when 'Maturity' then 2.0 when 'Retention' then 1.8 when 'Activation' then 1.2 else 1.0 end),2)::decimal(18,2) as estimated_customer_ltv,
       case when customer_health_score>=4.5 then 0.95 when customer_health_score>=4 then 0.85 when customer_health_score>=3.5 then 0.75 when customer_health_score>=3 then 0.65 when customer_health_score>=2.5 then 0.50 when customer_health_score>=2 then 0.35 else 0.20 end::decimal(3,2) as retention_probability,
       case when customer_health_score>=4.5 then 0.05 when customer_health_score>=4 then 0.15 when customer_health_score>=3.5 then 0.25 when customer_health_score>=3 then 0.35 when customer_health_score>=2.5 then 0.50 when customer_health_score>=2 then 0.65 else 0.80 end::decimal(3,2) as churn_probability
    from health
), outputs as (
    select *, round(estimated_customer_value*churn_probability,2)::decimal(9,2) as revenue_at_risk,
       case when lifecycle_stage in ('Acquisition','Activation') and customer_health_score>=3.5 then 'High Growth Potential'
            when lifecycle_stage='Growth' and platform_consistency_score>=2 then 'Expansion Ready'
            when lifecycle_stage='Maturity' and customer_health_score>=4 then 'Upsell Candidate'
            when lifecycle_stage='Retention' and customer_health_score>=3 then 'Stable Account'
            when lifecycle_stage='Dormant' then 'Reactivation Needed' else 'Monitor' end as growth_potential,
       case when churn_probability>=0.65 then 5 when lifecycle_stage='Acquisition' and customer_health_score>=3.5 then 4
            when lifecycle_stage='Growth' and platform_consistency_score>=2 then 4
            when customer_health_score>=4 and estimated_customer_value>=3000 then 3
            when churn_probability>=0.35 then 3 else 2 end as action_priority
    from measures
), completed as (
    select *, case when month(acquisition_cohort_month) in (11,12,1) then 'Holiday Season'
       when month(acquisition_cohort_month) in (6,7,8) then 'Summer Season'
       when month(acquisition_cohort_month) in (3,4,5) then 'Spring Season' else 'Fall Season' end as acquisition_season,
       case when estimated_customer_ltv>=8000 then 'Platinum' when estimated_customer_ltv>=5000 then 'Gold'
            when estimated_customer_ltv>=2500 then 'Silver' when estimated_customer_ltv>=1000 then 'Bronze' else 'Basic' end as customer_tier,
       case when estimated_customer_ltv>=10000 or (customer_segment in ('Champion','Loyal Customer') and platform_consistency_score=3) then true else false end as is_strategic_account,
       case when estimated_customer_ltv>=8000 then 0.90 when estimated_customer_ltv>=5000 then 0.85
            when estimated_customer_ltv>=2500 and lifecycle_stage<>'Dormant' then 0.75
            when estimated_customer_ltv>=1000 and lifecycle_stage in ('Growth','Maturity') then 0.60 else 0.45 end::decimal(3,2) as expected_retention_rate
    from outputs
)
select marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id, primary_email, primary_organization,
 customer_first_touchpoint, customer_last_activity, account_age_days, customer_segment, customer_journey_pattern,
 days_since_last_activity, active_30_days, active_60_days, active_90_days, active_180_days, active_365_days,
 lifecycle_stage, acquisition_cohort_month, platform_consistency_score, estimated_customer_value,
 frequency_score, recency_score, estimated_transaction_count, customer_health_score, estimated_customer_ltv,
 retention_probability, churn_probability, revenue_at_risk,
 case when acquisition_cohort_month is not null then year(acquisition_cohort_month)::bigint end as acquisition_year,
 case when acquisition_cohort_month is not null then month(acquisition_cohort_month)::bigint end as acquisition_month,
 case when acquisition_cohort_month is not null then date_diff('month',acquisition_cohort_month::date,current_date)::bigint end as months_since_acquisition,
 acquisition_season, customer_tier, is_strategic_account,
 case action_priority when 5 then 'Immediate' when 4 then 'This Week' when 3 then 'This Month' else 'Routine' end as intervention_urgency,
 expected_retention_rate,
 case when retention_probability>expected_retention_rate then 'Above Expectation'
      when retention_probability>=expected_retention_rate*0.8 then 'Meeting Expectation' else 'Below Expectation' end as performance_vs_expectation,
 growth_potential, action_priority
from completed
```

```sql
 round(activity_decline_risk*.2+platform_abandonment_risk*.15+lifecycle_transition_risk*.15+email_engagement_risk*.1+payment_behavior_risk*.25+account_stability_risk*.1+revenue_at_risk_score*.05,2) as total_risk_score
```

```sql
WITH daily_stats AS (
    SELECT * FROM staging.stg_google_ads__account_stats
),
rolling_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        avg(spend) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id, source_relation ORDER BY date_day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS spend_7d_avg,
        avg(clicks) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id, source_relation ORDER BY date_day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS clicks_7d_avg,
        avg(impressions) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id, source_relation ORDER BY date_day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS impressions_7d_avg,
        lag(spend, 30) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id, source_relation ORDER BY date_day) AS spend_lag_30d,
        lag(conversions, 30) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id, source_relation ORDER BY date_day) AS conversions_lag_30d,
        min(date_day) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id) AS first_activity_date
    FROM daily_stats
),
metrics AS (
    SELECT *,
        round(CASE WHEN impressions > 0 THEN clicks::DOUBLE / impressions * 100 ELSE 0 END, 4)::FLOAT AS ctr,
        round(CASE WHEN clicks > 0 THEN spend / clicks ELSE 0 END, 4) AS cpc,
        round(CASE WHEN impressions > 0 THEN spend / impressions * 1000 ELSE 0 END, 4) AS cpm,
        round(CASE WHEN conversions > 0 THEN spend / conversions END, 4) AS cost_per_conversion,
        round(CASE WHEN spend > 0 AND conversions_value > 0 THEN conversions_value / spend ELSE 0 END, 4) AS roas,
        greatest(date_diff('day', first_activity_date, date_day), 0) AS days_since_first_activity
    FROM rolling_metrics
),
scored AS (
    SELECT *,
        round(CASE WHEN spend_lag_30d > 0 THEN (spend - spend_lag_30d) / spend_lag_30d * 100 END, 2) AS spend_mom_change_pct,
        round(CASE WHEN conversions_lag_30d > 0 THEN (conversions - conversions_lag_30d) / conversions_lag_30d * 100 END, 2) AS conversions_mom_change_pct,
        CASE WHEN ctr IS NULL OR roas IS NULL OR clicks_7d_avg IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE least(100.0, greatest(0.0, ctr * 10 + least(roas * 10, 50) + CASE WHEN cost_per_conversion < 50 THEN 20 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN clicks_7d_avg > 100 THEN 10 ELSE clicks_7d_avg / 10 END)) END AS performance_score,
        CASE WHEN days_since_first_activity < 30 THEN 'New Account' WHEN days_since_first_activity < 90 THEN 'Growing Account' WHEN days_since_first_activity < 365 THEN 'Established Account' ELSE 'Mature Account' END AS account_maturity_stage,
        (spend > 0 AND clicks = 0) AS has_spend_no_clicks_flag,
        (clicks > impressions) AS invalid_metrics_flag,
        (spend > 10000) AS high_spend_alert_flag
    FROM metrics
),
with_tier AS (
    SELECT *, CASE WHEN performance_score >= 80 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN performance_score >= 60 THEN 'Good' WHEN performance_score >= 40 THEN 'Average' WHEN performance_score >= 20 THEN 'Below Average' ELSE 'Poor' END AS performance_tier
    FROM scored
)
SELECT
    s.source_relation, s.account_id, a.account_name, a.currency_code, a.time_zone, s.date_day,
    s.spend, s.clicks, s.impressions, s.conversions, s.conversions_value, s.ctr, s.cpc, s.cpm,
    s.cost_per_conversion, s.roas, s.spend_7d_avg, s.clicks_7d_avg, s.impressions_7d_avg,
    s.spend_mom_change_pct, s.conversions_mom_change_pct, s.days_since_first_activity,
    s.account_maturity_stage, s.performance_score, s.performance_tier,
    s.has_spend_no_clicks_flag, s.invalid_metrics_flag, s.high_spend_alert_flag
FROM with_tier s
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_google_ads__account_history a
  ON s.account_id = a.account_id AND s.source_relation = a.source_relation AND a.is_most_recent_record
WHERE s.spend >= 0 AND s.clicks >= 0 AND s.impressions >= 0 AND s.conversions >= 0
  AND s.date_day IS NOT NULL AND s.account_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY s.account_id, s.date_day
```
